# star_toml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#star_toml--load-layer-and-validate-any-toml-config-file)star_toml — load, layer, and validate any `*.toml` config file

`star_toml` (pronounced “star TOML”, as in `*.toml`) is a self-contained
Rust framework for any TOML configuration file. Three concerns, one crate:

- **Loading**— parse a single file, compose multiple sources in layers, expand- `${ENV_VARS}`, walk parent dirs to discover config files.
- **Validation**— Pydantic-style engine that collects- *every*error at once, each with a path-precise location, the offending value, and a machine-matchable code.
- **Analytics**— Van der Aalst-grade extensions: conformance fitness, variant fingerprinting, DECLARE cross-field constraints, severity stratification.

Dependencies: `serde`, `toml`, `thiserror`. No async, no proc-macros, no allocator
tricks, no crypto.

[§](https://docs.rs#decision-guide--which-api-for-which-task)Decision guide — which API for which task?

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| Parse a TOML string | `from_str::<T>(s)` |
| Load one file | `load_file::<T>(path)` |
| Walk parent dirs to find a file | /`find_config_file``find_and_load` |
| Merge defaults + file + env | builder`Loader` |
| Remember where the file is (relative paths) | →`Loader::load_file``ConfigFile<T>` |
| Parse + validate in one call | `Loader::load_validated` |
| Serialize back to TOML | /`to_string``save_file` |
| Recursive table merge | `deep_merge` |
| `${VAR}`substitution alone | `expand_env_vars` |
| Validate an already-loaded struct | /`Validate::check``Validate::validated` |
| Validate without a Rust struct | declarative builder`Schema` |
| Attach severity / cross-field rules | /`Validator::with_severity``Validator::check_consistent` |
| Get conformance score | `ValidationErrors::fitness` |
| Fingerprint error pattern | `ValidationErrors::variant_id` |

[§](https://docs.rs#loading)Loading

| Symbol | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from_str` | fn | Expand env vars, parse TOML, deserialize to `T` |

[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-4--collect-all-errors-render-pydantic-style)Pattern 4 — collect all errors, render Pydantic-style

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Server { host: String, port: u16 }
struct App { name: String, workers: u32, server: Server }
impl Validate for Server {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("host", &self.host);
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1..=65535);
    }
}
impl Validate for App {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("name", &self.name);
        v.check_range("workers", self.workers, 1..=1024);
        v.field("server", |v| self.server.validate(v)); // nested → server.*
    }
}
let app = App {
    name: String::new(),
    workers: 0,
    server: Server { host: String::new(), port: 0 },
};
let report = app.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(report.len(), 4); // ALL four errors, not just the first
let locs: Vec<String> = report.errors().iter().map(|e| e.loc.to_string()).collect();
assert_eq!(locs, ["name", "workers", "server.host", "server.port"]);
// Renders as:
// 4 validation errors for App
// name
//   must not be empty (got: `""`) [empty]
// ...
println!("{report}");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-5--severity-levels--repair-hints)Pattern 5 — severity levels + repair hints

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator, Severity};
struct Cfg { log_dir: String, port: u16 }
impl Validate for Cfg {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        // Hard error: port is required
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
        // Advisory: non-critical best-practice hint
        v.with_severity(Severity::Advisory, |v| {
            v.check_non_empty("log_dir", &self.log_dir);
        });
    }
}
let errs = Cfg { port: 0, log_dir: String::new() }.check().unwrap_err();
assert!(!errs.has_fatal());
for e in errs.errors() {
    println!("[{}] {} → fix: {}", e.severity, e.loc, e.repair_hint());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-6--van-der-aalst-analytics)Pattern 6 — Van der Aalst analytics

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Pair { a: u32, b: u32 }
impl Validate for Pair {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("a", self.a, 1..=10); // passes
        v.check_range("b", self.b, 1..=10); // fails
    }
}
let errs = Pair { a: 5, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err();
// Conformance fitness: how much of the model the config satisfies
assert_eq!(errs.fitness(), 0.5); // 1 of 2 checks passed
// Variant fingerprint: same error pattern = same ID across runs
let id = errs.variant_id();
assert_eq!(Pair { a: 9, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err().variant_id(), id);
// Object-centric grouping: errors by top-level config section
for (section, errors) in errs.by_section() {
    println!("{section}: {} error(s)", errors.len());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-7--declare-cross-field-constraint)Pattern 7 — DECLARE cross-field constraint

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Tls { enabled: bool, cert_path: String }
impl Validate for Tls {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        // Co-existence: TLS enabled ⟺ cert_path non-empty
        v.check_consistent(
            "cert_path",            // primary field (where error is recorded)
            &["enabled"],           // related fields (tagged in ErrorKind::Inconsistent)
            !self.enabled || !self.cert_path.is_empty(),
            "tls_cert_required",    // stable machine-matchable code
            "cert_path must be set when TLS is enabled",
        );
    }
}
let bad = Tls { enabled: true, cert_path: String::new() };
let errs = bad.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].code(), "tls_cert_required");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-8--validate-arrays-element-by-element)Pattern 8 — validate arrays element-by-element

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Pipeline(Vec<String>);
impl Validate for Pipeline {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        for (i, stage) in self.0.iter().enumerate() {
            v.index(i, |v| v.check_non_empty("name", stage));
        }
    }
}
let p = Pipeline(vec!["build".into(), String::new(), "test".into()]);
let errs = p.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].loc.to_string(), "[1].name");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-9--source-relative-path-resolution)Pattern 9 — source-relative path resolution

```
use star_toml::{Loader, ConfigFile};
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Build { template_dir: String }
let cf: ConfigFile<Build> = Loader::new().find_file("build.toml").load_file()?;
// Resolved relative to the directory that contains build.toml,
// not relative to the current working directory.
let abs = cf.resolve(&cf.config.template_dir);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-10--write-back)Pattern 10 — write-back

```
use star_toml::save_file;
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
struct Config { name: String, port: u16 }
save_file(&Config { name: "app".into(), port: 8080 }, "ggen.toml")?;
// Parent directories are created automatically.
```
[§](https://docs.rs#layer-merge-semantics)Layer merge semantics

Layers merge left-to-right (later = higher priority).

- **Tables**: keys merged recursively — a later layer overrides one key without erasing siblings.
- **Arrays, scalars**: later layer replaces earlier entirely.

```
use toml::Value;
use star_toml::deep_merge;
let mut base: Value = toml::from_str("[db]\nhost=\"localhost\"\nport=5432\n").unwrap();
let overlay: Value = toml::from_str("[db]\nport=5433\n").unwrap();
deep_merge(&mut base, overlay);
// host preserved, port overridden
assert_eq!(base["db"]["host"].as_str(), Some("localhost"));
assert_eq!(base["db"]["port"].as_integer(), Some(5433));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#environment-variable-mapping)Environment variable mapping

`.env_prefix("APP_")` maps env vars to TOML keys:

- Prefix stripped: `APP_PORT`→`port`
- Double underscore as dot: `APP_SERVER__PORT`→`server.port`
- Value coercion: `"true"`→ bool,`"42"`→ integer,`"3.14"`→ float, otherwise string

Inline `${VAR}` / `$VAR` patterns in TOML sources are expanded before parsing.
Unknown variables are left as-is (safe for partial expansion).

```
use star_toml::expand_env_vars;
std::env::set_var("MY_HOST", "prod.example.com");
let out = expand_env_vars("host = \"${MY_HOST}\"");
assert_eq!(out, "host = \"prod.example.com\"");
std::env::remove_var("MY_HOST");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling)Error handling

All fallible free functions return [ Result<T>](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html) =

`Result<T, Error>`.
The most common error is [from](https://docs.rs/error/enum.Error.html#variant.Invalid)

`Error::Invalid`[; downcast with](https://docs.rs/loader/struct.Loader.html#method.load_validated)

`Loader::load_validated``if let Error::Invalid(report) = err { … }`.```
use star_toml::{Loader, Validate, Validator, Error};
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Cfg { port: u16 }
impl Validate for Cfg {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
    }
}
match Loader::new().find_file("server.toml").load_validated::<Cfg>() {
    Ok(cfg) => println!("port = {}", cfg.port),
    Err(Error::FileNotFound(p)) => eprintln!("config not found: {}", p.display()),
    Err(Error::Parse { source, .. }) => eprintln!("TOML syntax: {source}"),
    Err(Error::Invalid(report)) => {
        eprintln!("{report}");
        for e in report.errors() {
            eprintln!("  fix {} → {}", e.loc, e.repair_hint());
        }
    }
    Err(e) => eprintln!("other error: {e}"),
}
```

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/src/star_toml/lib.rs.html

# star_toml/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # star_toml — load, layer, and validate any `*.toml` config file
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! `star_toml` (pronounced "star TOML", as in `*.toml`) is a self-contained
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! Rust framework for any TOML configuration file. Three concerns, one crate:
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! 1. **Loading** — parse a single file, compose multiple sources in layers, expand
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!    `${ENV_VARS}`, walk parent dirs to discover config files.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! 2. **Validation** — Pydantic-style engine that collects *every* error at once, each
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!    with a path-precise location, the offending value, and a machine-matchable code.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! 3. **Analytics** — Van der Aalst-grade extensions: conformance fitness, variant
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!    fingerprinting, DECLARE cross-field constraints, severity stratification.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! Dependencies: `serde`, `toml`, `thiserror`. No async, no proc-macros, no allocator
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! tricks, no crypto.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! ---
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! ## Decision guide — which API for which task?
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! | Task | Use |
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! |------|-----|
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! | Parse a TOML string | [`from_str::<T>(s)`](from_str) |
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! | Load one file | [`load_file::<T>(path)`](load_file) |
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! | Walk parent dirs to find a file | [`find_config_file`] / [`find_and_load`] |
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! | Merge defaults + file + env | [`Loader`] builder |
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! | Remember where the file is (relative paths) | [`Loader::load_file`] → [`ConfigFile<T>`] |
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! | Parse + validate in one call | [`Loader::load_validated`] |
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! | Serialize back to TOML | [`to_string`] / [`save_file`] |
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! | Recursive table merge | [`deep_merge`] |
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! | `${VAR}` substitution alone | [`expand_env_vars`] |
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! | Validate an already-loaded struct | [`Validate::check`] / [`Validate::validated`] |
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! | Validate without a Rust struct | [`Schema`] declarative builder |
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! | Attach severity / cross-field rules | [`Validator::with_severity`] / [`Validator::check_consistent`] |
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! | Get conformance score | [`ValidationErrors::fitness`] |
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! | Fingerprint error pattern | [`ValidationErrors::variant_id`] |
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! ---
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! ## Complete public API
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! ### Loading
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! | Symbol | Kind | Description |
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! |--------|------|-------------|
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! | [`from_str`] | fn | Expand env vars, parse TOML, deserialize to `T` |
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! | [`load_file`] | fn | Read, expand, parse a `.toml` file |
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! | [`find_config_file`] | fn | Walk parent dirs for `name`; returns `Option<PathBuf>` |
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! | [`find_and_load`] | fn | [`find_config_file`] + [`load_file`] combined |
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! | [`Loader`] | struct | Builder: chain `.layer_str`, `.find_file`, `.env_prefix`, then `.load()` |
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! | [`ConfigFile<T>`] | struct | Loaded config + path; `.resolve(rel)` anchors relative paths |
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! | [`to_string`] | fn | Serialize `T: Serialize` to a TOML string |
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! | [`save_file`] | fn | Serialize to disk, creating parent dirs as needed |
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! | [`deep_merge`] | fn | Recursively merge two `toml::Value`s (later wins) |
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! | [`expand_env_vars`] | fn | `${VAR}` / `$VAR` substitution; unknown vars left intact |
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! ### Validation (Pydantic + Van der Aalst)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! | Symbol | Kind | Description |
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! |--------|------|-------------|
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! | [`Schema`] | struct | Declarative builder: validate `toml::Value` / TOML strings without a Rust struct |
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! | [`FieldBuilder`] | struct | Fluent constraint chain returned by [`Schema::field`] |
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! | [`Validate`] | trait | Implement `validate(&self, v: &mut Validator)` on your config type |
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! | [`Validator`] | struct | Accumulates errors; carries the current path location |
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! | [`Validator::field`] | method | Descend into table key `name` for the duration of a closure |
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! | [`Validator::index`] | method | Descend into array index `i` for the duration of a closure |
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! | [`Validator::with_severity`] | method | Set [`Severity`] for all checks inside a closure |
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! | [`Validator::check_non_empty`] | method | Fail if `&str` is empty → code `empty` |
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! | [`Validator::check_range`] | method | Fail if value outside `lo..=hi` → code `out_of_range` |
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! | [`Validator::check_one_of`] | method | Fail if value not in allowed set → code `not_one_of` |
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! | [`Validator::check_predicate`] | method | Custom boolean check with caller-defined code |
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! | [`Validator::check_consistent`] | method | DECLARE cross-field constraint → code `Inconsistent` |
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! | [`Validator::error`] | method | Record a raw [`ErrorKind`] at the current location |
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! | [`Validator::error_with`] | method | Same, capturing the offending value as a string |
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! | [`Validator::finish`] | method | Consume validator → `Ok(())` or `Err(ValidationErrors)` |
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! | [`ValidationErrors`] | struct | Non-empty collection of failures; implements `Display` + `Error` |
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! | [`ValidationErrors::errors`] | method | Slice of individual [`ValidationError`]s |
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! | [`ValidationErrors::len`] | method | Error count |
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! | [`ValidationErrors::fitness`] | method | Conformance score: `checks_passed / checks_run` (0.0–1.0) |
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! | [`ValidationErrors::variant_id`] | method | FNV-1a fingerprint of the error pattern |
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! | [`ValidationErrors::by_section`] | method | Group errors by top-level config section |
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! | [`ValidationErrors::has_fatal`] | method | True if any error is `Severity::Fatal` |
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! | [`ValidationErrors::errors_above`] | method | Filter to errors at or above a severity level |
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! | [`ValidationError`] | struct | One failure: `loc`, `kind`, `severity`, `input`, `msg` |
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! | [`ValidationError::code`] | method | Stable string code (`"empty"`, `"out_of_range"`, …) |
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! | [`ValidationError::repair_hint`] | method | Auto-derived minimum fix for this error kind |
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! | [`ValidationError::is_fatal`] | method | True when `severity == Severity::Fatal` |
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! | [`ErrorKind`] | enum | Structured reason: `Empty`, `OutOfRange`, `NotOneOf`, `Inconsistent`, … |
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! | [`Loc`] | struct | Path into the config tree, e.g. `server.tls.port` or `[2].name` |
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! | [`LocSegment`] | enum | `Key(String)` or `Index(usize)` |
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! | [`Severity`] | enum | `Advisory` < `Warning` < `Error` < `Fatal` |
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! ### Error types
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! | Variant | When |
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! |---------|------|
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! | [`Error::FileNotFound`] | File does not exist |
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! | [`Error::Io`] | OS error reading / writing a file |
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! | [`Error::Parse`] | TOML syntax or serde deserialization error |
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! | [`Error::Serialize`] | `toml::to_string` failed |
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! | [`Error::Invalid`] | Wraps [`ValidationErrors`]; returned by [`Loader::load_validated`] |
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! | [`Error::Validation`] | Lower-level validation string; rarely produced by this crate |
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//!
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! ---
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! ## Patterns cookbook (copy-pasteable)
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//!
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! ### Pattern 1 — load a single file
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//!
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! ```no_run
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! use star_toml::load_file;
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//!
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! struct AppConfig { name: String, port: u16 }
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! let cfg: AppConfig = load_file("app.toml")?;
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! # Ok::<(), star_toml::Error>(())
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! ```
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! ### Pattern 2 — layered loading (defaults + file + env)
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//! ```no_run
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//! use star_toml::Loader;
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//! #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! struct Cfg { name: String, port: u16 }
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//! const DEFAULTS: &str = "name = 'my-app'\nport = 8080\n";
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//! let cfg: Cfg = Loader::new()
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//!     .layer_str(DEFAULTS, "built-in defaults")  // lowest priority
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!     .find_file("app.toml")                      // walk up from cwd
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//!     .layer_file_if_exists("~/.config/app.toml") // optional user overrides
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!     .env_prefix("APP_")                         // APP_PORT=9090 → port = 9090
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!     .load()?;                                   // highest priority
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! # Ok::<(), star_toml::Error>(())
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//! ```
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! ### Pattern 3 — load + validate in one call
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//! ```no_run
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//! use star_toml::{Loader, Validate, Validator};
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//! #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//! struct Cfg { port: u16 }
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//! impl Validate for Cfg {
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//!         v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!     }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! }
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! // Fails with Error::Invalid(ValidationErrors) if any rule is violated.
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! let cfg: Cfg = Loader::new().find_file("server.toml").load_validated()?;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! # Ok::<(), star_toml::Error>(())
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! ```
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//!
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! ### Pattern 4 — collect all errors, render Pydantic-style
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//!
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//! ```
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//! struct Server { host: String, port: u16 }
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//! struct App { name: String, workers: u32, server: Server }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//! impl Validate for Server {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!         v.check_non_empty("host", &self.host);
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//!         v.check_range("port", self.port, 1..=65535);
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!     }
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! impl Validate for App {
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!         v.check_non_empty("name", &self.name);
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!         v.check_range("workers", self.workers, 1..=1024);
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!         v.field("server", |v| self.server.validate(v)); // nested → server.*
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!     }
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! }
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//!
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! let app = App {
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!     name: String::new(),
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//!     workers: 0,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!     server: Server { host: String::new(), port: 0 },
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! };
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! let report = app.check().unwrap_err();
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! assert_eq!(report.len(), 4); // ALL four errors, not just the first
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//!
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! let locs: Vec<String> = report.errors().iter().map(|e| e.loc.to_string()).collect();
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! assert_eq!(locs, ["name", "workers", "server.host", "server.port"]);
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//!
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! // Renders as:
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! // 4 validation errors for App
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! // name
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! //   must not be empty (got: `""`) [empty]
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! // ...
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! println!("{report}");
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! ```
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//!
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//! ### Pattern 5 — severity levels + repair hints
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//!
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! ```
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//! use star_toml::{Validate, Validator, Severity};
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//!
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! struct Cfg { log_dir: String, port: u16 }
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! impl Validate for Cfg {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//!         // Hard error: port is required
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//!         v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!         // Advisory: non-critical best-practice hint
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//!         v.with_severity(Severity::Advisory, |v| {
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//!             v.check_non_empty("log_dir", &self.log_dir);
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//!         });
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!     }
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//!
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! let errs = Cfg { port: 0, log_dir: String::new() }.check().unwrap_err();
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//! assert!(!errs.has_fatal());
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//!
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! for e in errs.errors() {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//!     println!("[{}] {} → fix: {}", e.severity, e.loc, e.repair_hint());
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//! }
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! ```
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! ### Pattern 6 — Van der Aalst analytics
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//!
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//! ```
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//! use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//! struct Pair { a: u32, b: u32 }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! impl Validate for Pair {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//!         v.check_range("a", self.a, 1..=10); // passes
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//!         v.check_range("b", self.b, 1..=10); // fails
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//!     }
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//! }
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//!
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//! let errs = Pair { a: 5, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err();
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//!
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//! // Conformance fitness: how much of the model the config satisfies
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//! assert_eq!(errs.fitness(), 0.5); // 1 of 2 checks passed
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//!
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//! // Variant fingerprint: same error pattern = same ID across runs
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//! let id = errs.variant_id();
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//! assert_eq!(Pair { a: 9, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err().variant_id(), id);
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//!
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//! // Object-centric grouping: errors by top-level config section
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//! for (section, errors) in errs.by_section() {
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//!     println!("{section}: {} error(s)", errors.len());
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//! }
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//! ```
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//!
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//! ### Pattern 7 — DECLARE cross-field constraint
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//!
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! ```
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//! use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//!
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//! struct Tls { enabled: bool, cert_path: String }
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//!
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//! impl Validate for Tls {
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//!         // Co-existence: TLS enabled ⟺ cert_path non-empty
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//!         v.check_consistent(
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//!             "cert_path",            // primary field (where error is recorded)
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//!             &["enabled"],           // related fields (tagged in ErrorKind::Inconsistent)
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//!             !self.enabled || !self.cert_path.is_empty(),
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//!             "tls_cert_required",    // stable machine-matchable code
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//!             "cert_path must be set when TLS is enabled",
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//!         );
[270](https://docs.rs#270)//!     }
[271](https://docs.rs#271)//! }
[272](https://docs.rs#272)//!
[273](https://docs.rs#273)//! let bad = Tls { enabled: true, cert_path: String::new() };
[274](https://docs.rs#274)//! let errs = bad.check().unwrap_err();
[275](https://docs.rs#275)//! assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].code(), "tls_cert_required");
[276](https://docs.rs#276)//! ```
[277](https://docs.rs#277)//!
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//! ### Pattern 8 — validate arrays element-by-element
[279](https://docs.rs#279)//!
[280](https://docs.rs#280)//! ```
[281](https://docs.rs#281)//! use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
[282](https://docs.rs#282)//!
[283](https://docs.rs#283)//! struct Pipeline(Vec<String>);
[284](https://docs.rs#284)//!
[285](https://docs.rs#285)//! impl Validate for Pipeline {
[286](https://docs.rs#286)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)//!         for (i, stage) in self.0.iter().enumerate() {
[288](https://docs.rs#288)//!             v.index(i, |v| v.check_non_empty("name", stage));
[289](https://docs.rs#289)//!         }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)//!     }
[291](https://docs.rs#291)//! }
[292](https://docs.rs#292)//!
[293](https://docs.rs#293)//! let p = Pipeline(vec!["build".into(), String::new(), "test".into()]);
[294](https://docs.rs#294)//! let errs = p.check().unwrap_err();
[295](https://docs.rs#295)//! assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].loc.to_string(), "[1].name");
[296](https://docs.rs#296)//! ```
[297](https://docs.rs#297)//!
[298](https://docs.rs#298)//! ### Pattern 9 — source-relative path resolution
[299](https://docs.rs#299)//!
[300](https://docs.rs#300)//! ```no_run

[312](https://docs.rs#312)//!

[314](https://docs.rs#314)//!
[315](https://docs.rs#315)//! ```no_run

[325](https://docs.rs#325)//!
[326](https://docs.rs#326)//! ---
[327](https://docs.rs#327)//!
[328](https://docs.rs#328)//! ## Layer merge semantics
[329](https://docs.rs#329)//!
[330](https://docs.rs#330)//! Layers merge left-to-right (later = higher priority).
[331](https://docs.rs#331)//! - **Tables**: keys merged recursively — a later layer overrides one key without erasing siblings.
[332](https://docs.rs#332)//! - **Arrays, scalars**: later layer replaces earlier entirely.
[333](https://docs.rs#333)//!
[334](https://docs.rs#334)//! ```
[335](https://docs.rs#335)//! use toml::Value;
[336](https://docs.rs#336)//! use star_toml::deep_merge;
[337](https://docs.rs#337)//!
[338](https://docs.rs#338)//! let mut base: Value = toml::from_str("[db]\nhost=\"localhost\"\nport=5432\n").unwrap();
[339](https://docs.rs#339)//! let overlay: Value = toml::from_str("[db]\nport=5433\n").unwrap();
[340](https://docs.rs#340)//! deep_merge(&mut base, overlay);
[341](https://docs.rs#341)//! // host preserved, port overridden
[342](https://docs.rs#342)//! assert_eq!(base["db"]["host"].as_str(), Some("localhost"));
[343](https://docs.rs#343)//! assert_eq!(base["db"]["port"].as_integer(), Some(5433));
[344](https://docs.rs#344)//! ```
[345](https://docs.rs#345)//!
[346](https://docs.rs#346)//! ## Environment variable mapping
[347](https://docs.rs#347)//!
[348](https://docs.rs#348)//! `.env_prefix("APP_")` maps env vars to TOML keys:
[349](https://docs.rs#349)//! - Prefix stripped: `APP_PORT` → `port`
[350](https://docs.rs#350)//! - Double underscore as dot: `APP_SERVER__PORT` → `server.port`
[351](https://docs.rs#351)//! - Value coercion: `"true"` → bool, `"42"` → integer, `"3.14"` → float, otherwise string
[352](https://docs.rs#352)//!
[353](https://docs.rs#353)//! Inline `${VAR}` / `$VAR` patterns in TOML sources are expanded before parsing.
[354](https://docs.rs#354)//! Unknown variables are left as-is (safe for partial expansion).
[355](https://docs.rs#355)//!
[356](https://docs.rs#356)//! ```
[357](https://docs.rs#357)//! use star_toml::expand_env_vars;
[358](https://docs.rs#358)//!
[359](https://docs.rs#359)//! std::env::set_var("MY_HOST", "prod.example.com");
[360](https://docs.rs#360)//! let out = expand_env_vars("host = \"${MY_HOST}\"");
[361](https://docs.rs#361)//! assert_eq!(out, "host = \"prod.example.com\"");
[362](https://docs.rs#362)//! std::env::remove_var("MY_HOST");
[363](https://docs.rs#363)//! ```
[364](https://docs.rs#364)//!
[365](https://docs.rs#365)//! ---
[366](https://docs.rs#366)//!
[367](https://docs.rs#367)//! ## Error handling
[368](https://docs.rs#368)//!
[369](https://docs.rs#369)//! All fallible free functions return [`Result<T>`] = `Result<T, Error>`.
[370](https://docs.rs#370)//! The most common error is [`Error::Invalid`] from [`Loader::load_validated`];
[371](https://docs.rs#371)//! downcast with `if let Error::Invalid(report) = err { … }`.
[372](https://docs.rs#372)//!
[373](https://docs.rs#373)//! ```no_run
[374](https://docs.rs#374)//! use star_toml::{Loader, Validate, Validator, Error};
[375](https://docs.rs#375)//!
[376](https://docs.rs#376)//! #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
[377](https://docs.rs#377)//! struct Cfg { port: u16 }
[378](https://docs.rs#378)//! impl Validate for Cfg {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)//!     fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)//!         v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
[381](https://docs.rs#381)//!     }
[382](https://docs.rs#382)//! }
[383](https://docs.rs#383)//!
[384](https://docs.rs#384)//! match Loader::new().find_file("server.toml").load_validated::<Cfg>() {
[385](https://docs.rs#385)//!     Ok(cfg) => println!("port = {}", cfg.port),
[386](https://docs.rs#386)//!     Err(Error::FileNotFound(p)) => eprintln!("config not found: {}", p.display()),
[387](https://docs.rs#387)//!     Err(Error::Parse { source, .. }) => eprintln!("TOML syntax: {source}"),
[388](https://docs.rs#388)//!     Err(Error::Invalid(report)) => {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)//!         eprintln!("{report}");
[390](https://docs.rs#390)//!         for e in report.errors() {
[391](https://docs.rs#391)//!             eprintln!("  fix {} → {}", e.loc, e.repair_hint());
[392](https://docs.rs#392)//!         }
[393](https://docs.rs#393)//!     }
[394](https://docs.rs#394)//!     Err(e) => eprintln!("other error: {e}"),
[395](https://docs.rs#395)//! }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)//! # Ok::<(), star_toml::Error>(())
[397](https://docs.rs#397)//! ```
[398](https://docs.rs#398)
[399](https://docs.rs#399)pub mod error;
[400](https://docs.rs#400)pub mod expand;
[401](https://docs.rs#401)pub mod loader;
[402](https://docs.rs#402)pub mod merge;
[403](https://docs.rs#403)pub mod schema;
[404](https://docs.rs#404)pub mod validation;

# Loader in star_toml::loader - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/loader/struct.Loader.html

`pub struct Loader { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Builder for composing multiple TOML config sources into a single value.

Sources are merged in the order they are added: earlier layers provide defaults, later layers override specific keys. Table keys are merged recursively; arrays and scalars are replaced entirely by the later layer.

Environment-variable expansion (`${VAR}` / `$VAR`) is applied to every source
before parsing.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use star_toml::Loader;
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct AppConfig {
    name: String,
}
const DEFAULTS: &str = r#"
name = "default-app"
"#;
let cfg: AppConfig = Loader::new()
    .layer_str(DEFAULTS, "built-in defaults")
    .find_file("app.toml")       // walks up from cwd
    .env_prefix("APP_")          // APP_NAME=foo → name = "foo"
    .load()?;
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Add a literal TOML string as the next layer.

`label` is used in error messages to identify this source (e.g., `"built-in defaults"`).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/loader.rs.html#177-180)#### pub fn [layer_file_if_exists](https://docs.rs#method.layer_file_if_exists)(self, path: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)>) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/loader.rs.html#177-180)

#### pub fn [layer_file_if_exists](https://docs.rs#method.layer_file_if_exists)(self, path: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)>) -> Self

Add a TOML file as the next layer, silently skipping it when absent.

Useful for optional user-specific config files (e.g., `~/.config/app.toml`).

Walk parent directories from the current working directory until `file_name`
is found, then add that file as the next layer.

Skipped silently when the file is not found anywhere in the directory tree.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/loader.rs.html#207-210)#### pub fn [env_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.env_prefix)(self, prefix: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/loader.rs.html#207-210)

#### pub fn [env_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.env_prefix)(self, prefix: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>) -> Self

Apply environment-variable overrides using `prefix` as a filter.

After loading and merging all file layers, any env var whose name starts with
`prefix` is stripped of that prefix and mapped to a TOML key path:

- Double underscores (`__`) become`.`(path separator)
- The result is lowercased

For example, with prefix `"APP_"`:

- `APP_NAME=foo`→- `name = "foo"`
- `APP_SERVER__PORT=9090`→- `server.port = 9090`(integer)
- `APP_DEBUG=true`→- `debug = true`(boolean)

Values are parsed as TOML scalars: bool → integer → float → string.

# deep_merge in star_toml::merge - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/merge/fn.deep_merge.html

## Expand description

Recursively merge `overlay` into `base`.

- **Tables**: keys present in- `overlay`are inserted or recursively merged into- `base`. Keys absent from- `overlay`are left unchanged in- `base`.
- **Everything else**(arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, datetimes):- `overlay`replaces- `base`entirely.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use toml::Value;
use star_toml::deep_merge;
let mut base: Value = toml::from_str(r#"
[server]
host = "localhost"
port = 8080
"#).unwrap();
let overlay: Value = toml::from_str(r#"
[server]
port = 9090
"#).unwrap();
deep_merge(&mut base, overlay);
let tbl = base.as_table().unwrap();
let server = tbl["server"].as_table().unwrap();
assert_eq!(server["host"].as_str(), Some("localhost")); // preserved
assert_eq!(server["port"].as_integer(), Some(9090));    // overridden
```

# expand_env_vars in star_toml::expand - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/expand/fn.expand_env_vars.html

## Expand description

Expand `${VAR}` and `$VAR` references using the current process environment.

- Known variables are replaced with their value.
- Unknown variables are left as-is (safe for partial expansion).
- The surrounding TOML text is copied verbatim via string slices, so multi-byte
UTF-8 characters outside of `$…`expressions are never corrupted.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
std::env::set_var("STAR_HOME", "/opt/star");
let out = star_toml::expand_env_vars("path = \"${STAR_HOME}/config\"");
assert_eq!(out, "path = \"/opt/star/config\"");
std::env::remove_var("STAR_HOME");
```

}## Expand description

Implemented by config types that can check their own invariants.

Implement [ validate](https://docs.rs/trait.Validate.html#tymethod.validate) — record failures into the

[. The provided](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html)

`Validator`[and](https://docs.rs/trait.Validate.html#method.check)

`check`[methods run it and produce a titled](https://docs.rs/trait.Validate.html#method.validated)

`validated`[report.](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationErrors.html)

`ValidationErrors`Compose nested types with [ Validator::field](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html#method.field):

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Tls { cert_path: String }
struct Server { port: u16, tls: Option<Tls> }
impl Validate for Tls {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("cert_path", &self.cert_path);
    }
}
impl Validate for Server {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1..=65535);
        if let Some(tls) = &self.tls {
            v.field("tls", |v| tls.validate(v));   // nested errors → tls.cert_path
        }
    }
}
let s = Server { port: 0, tls: Some(Tls { cert_path: String::new() }) };
let errs = s.check().unwrap_err();
let locs: Vec<String> = errs.errors().iter().map(|e| e.loc.to_string()).collect();
assert_eq!(locs, ["port", "tls.cert_path"]);
```

Run `f` with the given severity applied to every error emitted inside it.

Severity resets to the enclosing scope’s value after `f` returns.

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator, Severity};
struct Config { log_dir: String }
impl Validate for Config {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        // Best-practice advisory: non-critical
        v.with_severity(Severity::Warning, |v| {
            v.check_non_empty("log_dir", &self.log_dir);
        });
    }
}
let errs = Config { log_dir: String::new() }.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].severity, Severity::Warning);
assert!(!errs.has_fatal());
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#724-736)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#724-736)

**DECLARE-style cross-field constraint** (Van der Aalst).

Records an [ ErrorKind::Inconsistent](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.Inconsistent) at

`primary_field` when `condition`
is `false`, tagging `related_fields` as the other objects in the constraint.This models DECLARE’s *co-existence*, *response*, and *precedence*
templates: field A is only valid in relation to field B.

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Tls { enabled: bool, cert_path: String }
impl Validate for Tls {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        // Co-existence: TLS enabled ⟺ cert_path non-empty
        v.check_consistent(
            "cert_path",
            &["enabled"],
            !self.enabled || !self.cert_path.is_empty(),
            "tls_cert_required",
            "cert_path must be set when TLS is enabled",
        );
    }
}
let bad = Tls { enabled: true, cert_path: String::new() };
let errs = bad.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].code(), "tls_cert_required");
```

#### pub fn [errors_above](https://docs.rs#method.errors_above)(
    &self,
    min: [Severity](https://docs.rs/enum.Severity.html),

Errors at or above the given severity threshold.

**Van der Aalst alignment fitness** — proportion of checks that passed.

Returns 1.0 when all checks pass (no errors), 0.0 when every check failed. Analogous to the replay-fitness metric from conformance checking: how well does the observed config align to the declared validation model?

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Pair { a: u32, b: u32 }
impl Validate for Pair {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("a", self.a, 1..=10);  // passes
        v.check_range("b", self.b, 1..=10);  // fails
    }
}
let errs = Pair { a: 5, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.fitness(), 0.5);  // 1 of 2 checks passed
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#490-498)#### pub fn [variant_id](https://docs.rs#method.variant_id)(&self) -> [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#490-498)

#### pub fn [variant_id](https://docs.rs#method.variant_id)(&self) -> [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

**Variant fingerprint** — a deterministic hash of the failure pattern.

Two `ValidationErrors` instances with the same set of `(location, code)`
pairs produce the same variant ID, regardless of message text or input
values. Useful for deduplicating recurring failure patterns across runs.

Uses FNV-1a over the sorted `"loc:code"` pairs.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#507-525)#### pub fn [by_section](https://docs.rs#method.by_section)(&self) -> [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[ValidationError](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationError.html)>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#507-525)

#### pub fn [by_section](https://docs.rs#method.by_section)(&self) -> [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[ValidationError](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationError.html)>>

**Object-centric grouping** — errors indexed by their top-level config section.

Implements Van der Aalst’s object-centric view: each top-level TOML table is an “object type”; this groups all its constraint violations together.

Root-level errors are keyed `"(root)"`.

# Severity in star_toml::validation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/validation/enum.Severity.html

```
pub enum Severity {
    Advisory,
    Warning,
    Error,
    Fatal,
}
```
## Expand description

How severe a validation failure is — ordered least to most severe.

The default for all `check_*` methods is [ Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Severity.html#variant.Error).
Use

[to override for a closure.](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html#method.with_severity)

`Validator::with_severity`Comparison: `Advisory < Warning < Error < Fatal`.

| Level | Meaning | `has_fatal` |
|---|---|---|
| `Advisory` | best-practice hint; config is usable | no |
| `Warning` | risky but technically valid | no |
| `Error` | constraint violated; config is broken | no |
| `Fatal` | unrecoverable; halt all evaluation | yes |

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator, Severity};
struct Cfg { log_dir: String }
impl Validate for Cfg {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.with_severity(Severity::Warning, |v| {
            v.check_non_empty("log_dir", &self.log_dir);
        });
    }
}
let errs = Cfg { log_dir: String::new() }.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].severity, Severity::Warning);
assert!(!errs.has_fatal());
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Advisory)

### Advisory

Informational: not a hard rule, but a best-practice recommendation.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Warning)

### Warning

Technically acceptable but risky or sub-optimal.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Error)

### Error

Constraint violated — the default level. Config is unusable.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fatal)

### Fatal

Unrecoverable: halt immediately, do not evaluate further constraints.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/star_toml/validation.rs.html#338-361)#### pub fn [repair_hint](https://docs.rs#method.repair_hint)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

#### pub fn [repair_hint](https://docs.rs#method.repair_hint)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

Auto-derived repair suggestion based on the error kind.

For custom predicates the message itself is the best hint; for built-in kinds the hint is derived from the constraint parameters.

This implements Van der Aalst’s *alignment repair* concept: given a
deviation from the reference model, what is the minimum edit?

The central piece of the `star_toml` framework. Each `layer_*` call adds one

# star_toml::schema - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/schema/index.html

## Expand description

Declarative `Schema` builder — validate any `toml::Value` without Rust structs.

The Pydantic + Van der Aalst engines in [ validation](https://docs.rs/validation/index.html) require
implementing

[for each config type. That’s powerful for typed configs — but sometimes you want to validate a raw TOML file without writing a struct at all.](https://docs.rs/validation/trait.Validate.html)

`Validate``Schema` is the 1,700× version: declare constraints once, validate any
`toml::Value` or TOML string directly.

[§](https://docs.rs#phase-shift-comparison)Phase-shift comparison

**Before (imperative  Validate):**

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct ServerConfig { host: String, port: u16 }
impl Validate for ServerConfig {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("host", &self.host);
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1..=65535);
    }
}
// Must deserialize to the struct first
let s = ServerConfig { host: String::new(), port: 0 };
let errs = s.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.len(), 2);
```
**After (declarative  Schema):**

```
use star_toml::Schema;
let schema = Schema::new()
    .field("host").non_empty().done()
    .field("port").range_i64(1, 65535).done();
let errs = schema.validate_str("[server]\nhost=''\nport=0").unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.len(), 2);
```
Each `.field()` call opens a [ FieldBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldBuilder.html); call

`.done()` to return to the
parent `Schema` before opening the next field.[§](https://docs.rs#nesting)Nesting

```
use star_toml::Schema;
let schema = Schema::new()
    .field("name").non_empty().done()
    .field("workers").range_i64(1, 1024).done()
    .section("server", Schema::new()
        .field("host").non_empty().done()
        .field("port").range_i64(1, 65535).done());
let toml = r#"
name = "demo"
workers = 8
[server]
host = "localhost"
port = 8080
"#;
assert!(schema.validate_str(toml).is_ok());
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldBuilder.html)- Builder
- Fluent builder returned by `Schema::field`
- [Schema](https://docs.rs/struct.Schema.html)
- Declarative validation schema for raw TOML values.

# star_toml::validation - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/validation/index.html

## Expand description

Pydantic-grade + Van der Aalst-grade validation for TOML configs.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Validation works by *descent*: implement [ Validate](https://docs.rs/trait.Validate.html) for each config type,
use a

[to record failures, and compose nested types with](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html)

`Validator`[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html#method.field)

`Validator::field`[. Every](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html#method.index)

`Validator::index``check_*` call is an
atomic “check event” — the validator counts all checks (pass + fail) for the
conformance score.[§](https://docs.rs#validator-method-reference)Validator method reference

[§](https://docs.rs#descent-path-tracking)Descent (path tracking)

| Method | Signature | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | `(name: &str, f: FnOnce(&mut Validator))` | Push key segment, run `f`, pop |
| `index` | `(i: usize, f: FnOnce(&mut Validator))` | Push index segment, run `f`, pop |

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-checks-each-counts-as-one-check-event)Built-in checks (each counts as one check event)

| Method | Code | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| `check_non_empty` | `empty` | `&str`is`""` |
| `check_range` | `out_of_range` | value outside `lo..=hi` |
| `check_one_of` | `not_one_of` | value not in allowed slice |
| `check_predicate` | caller-defined | boolean is `false` |
| `check_consistent` | caller-defined | cross-field condition is `false` |

[§](https://docs.rs#severity-control)Severity control

Default severity: [ Severity::Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Severity.html#variant.Error).
Errors with

`Severity < Error` (Warning / Advisory) still appear in the report
but do not block [.](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationErrors.html#method.has_fatal)

`ValidationErrors::has_fatal`[§](https://docs.rs#raw-error-recording)Raw error recording

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `error` | Record at the current location`ErrorKind` |
| `error_with` | Same, capturing the offending value as a string |
| `finish` | Consume the validator → `Ok(())`or`Err(ValidationErrors)` |

[§](https://docs.rs#validationerrors-analytics)ValidationErrors analytics

| Method | Returns | Van der Aalst concept |
|---|---|---|
| `errors` | `&[ValidationError]` | — |
| `fitness` | `f64`0.0–1.0 | Replay fitness / alignment score |
| `variant_id` | `u64` | Trace variant fingerprint |
| `by_section` | `BTreeMap<String, Vec<_>>` | OCEL object-centric view |
| `has_fatal` | `bool` | Halt-immediately signal |
| `errors_above` | `impl Iterator` | Severity filter |

[§](https://docs.rs#validationerror-fields)ValidationError fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loc` | `Loc` | Path, e.g. `server.tls.port`or`[2].name` |
| `kind` | `ErrorKind` | Structured reason (machine-matchable) |
| `severity` | `Severity` | Advisory / Warning / Error / Fatal |
| `input` | `Option<String>` | Offending value, if captured |
| `msg` | `String` | Human-readable message |

Plus: [ code()](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationError.html#method.code),

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationError.html#method.repair_hint)

`repair_hint()`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationError.html#method.is_fatal)

`is_fatal()`[§](https://docs.rs#errorkind-codes)ErrorKind codes

| Variant | `code()` | Produced by |
|---|---|---|
| `Missing` | `missing` | `error(ErrorKind::Missing, …)` |
| `Empty` | `empty` | `check_non_empty` |
| `OutOfRange` | `out_of_range` | `check_range` |
| `TooShort` | `too_short` | `error(ErrorKind::TooShort{…}, …)` |
| `TooLong` | `too_long` | `error(ErrorKind::TooLong{…}, …)` |
| `NotOneOf` | `not_one_of` | `check_one_of` |
| `Inconsistent` | caller-defined | `check_consistent` |
| `Predicate` | caller-defined | `check_predicate`,`error(ErrorKind::Predicate{…}, …)` |

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator, Severity};
struct Server { host: String, port: u16 }
impl Validate for Server {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("host", &self.host);
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1..=65535);
    }
}
let bad = Server { host: String::new(), port: 0 };
let errs = bad.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.len(), 2);
assert_eq!(errs.fitness(), 0.0);               // 0 of 2 checks passed
assert!(!errs.errors()[0].repair_hint().is_empty());
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Loc](https://docs.rs/struct.Loc.html)
- A path to a value in the config tree, rendered like `server.tls.port`or`stages[2].name`.
- [Validation](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationError.html)- Error
- A single validation failure at a precise `Loc`
- [Validation](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationErrors.html)- Errors
- A non-empty collection of `ValidationError`
- [Validator](https://docs.rs/struct.Validator.html)
- Accumulates errors while tracking the current location as you descend a config tree.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind

- [LocSegment](https://docs.rs/enum.LocSegment.html)

- [Severity](https://docs.rs/enum.Severity.html)

- `protoc`

# bincode - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bincode/^1.3/

## Expand description

Bincode is a crate for encoding and decoding using a tiny binary serialization strategy. Using it, you can easily go from having an object in memory, quickly serialize it to bytes, and then deserialize it back just as fast!

[§](https://docs.rs#using-basic-functions)Using Basic Functions

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    // The object that we will serialize.
    let target: Option<String>  = Some("hello world".to_string());
    let encoded: Vec<u8> = bincode::serialize(&target).unwrap();
    let decoded: Option<String> = bincode::deserialize(&encoded[..]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(target, decoded);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#128bit-numbers)128bit numbers

Support for `i128` and `u128` is automatically enabled on Rust toolchains
greater than or equal to `1.26.0` and disabled for targets which do not support it

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [Config](https://docs.rs/config/struct.Config.html);- Deprecated
- `pub use config::`- [DefaultOptions](https://docs.rs/config/struct.DefaultOptions.html);
- `pub use config::`- [Options](https://docs.rs/config/trait.Options.html);
- `pub use de::read::`- [BincodeRead](https://docs.rs/de/read/trait.BincodeRead.html);
- `pub use de::`- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/de/struct.Deserializer.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- `bincode`uses a Builder-pattern to configure the Serializers and Deserializers in this crate. This means that if you need to customize the behavior of- `bincode`, you should create an instance of the- `DefaultOptions`struct:
- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Deserialize bincode data to a Rust data structure.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/struct.Serializer.html)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [deserialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize_from.html)- from
- Deserializes an object directly from a `Read`er using the default configuration.
- [deserialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize_from_custom.html)- from_ - custom
- Deserializes an object from a custom `BincodeRead`er using the default configuration. It is highly recommended to use`deserialize_from`unless you need to implement`BincodeRead`for performance reasons.
- [options](https://docs.rs/fn.options.html)
- Get a default configuration object.
- [serialize](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize.html)
- Serializes a serializable object into a `Vec`of bytes using the default configuration.
- [serialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize_into.html)- into
- Serializes an object directly into a `Writer`using the default configuration.
- [serialized_](https://docs.rs/fn.serialized_size.html)- size
- Returns the size that an object would be if serialized using Bincode with the default configuration.
