Prepares a database batch containing the chain value pool update from `finalized.block`, and
returns it without actually writing anything.

The batch is modified by this method and written by the caller. The caller should not write the batch if this method returns an error.

The parameter `utxos_spent_by_block` must contain the [ transparent::Utxo](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transparent/utxo/struct.Utxo.html)s of every input
in this block, including UTXOs created by earlier transactions in this block.

Note that the chain value pool has the opposite sign to the transaction value pool. See the
[ chain_value_pool_change](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/struct.Block.html#method.chain_value_pool_change) and

[methods for more details.](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/value_balance/struct.ValueBalance.html#method.add_chain_value_pool_change)

`add_chain_value_pool_change`[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

- Propagates any errors from updating value pools

From state format 25.3.0 onwards, the Sprout trees are indexed by an empty key, so this method does nothing.

#### pub fn [prepare_new_transparent_outputs_batch](https://docs.rs#method.prepare_new_transparent_outputs_batch)(

    db: &DiskDb,
    network: &[Network](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/parameters/network/enum.Network.html),
    new_outputs_by_out_loc: &[BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<[OutputLocation](https://docs.rs/struct.OutputLocation.html), [Utxo](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transparent/utxo/struct.Utxo.html)>,
    address_balances: &AddressBalanceLocationUpdates,
)

Prepare a database batch for the new UTXOs in `new_outputs_by_out_loc`.

Adds the following changes to this batch:

- insert created UTXOs,
- insert transparent address UTXO index entries, and
- insert transparent address transaction entries,

without actually writing anything.

`address_balances` must already be populated for every transparent address that
receives one of these outputs (see
[ Self::prepare_transparent_address_balance_updates](https://docs.rs/struct.DiskWriteBatch.html#method.prepare_transparent_address_balance_updates)); this function only reads

`address_location()` from it.[§](https://docs.rs#errors-3)Errors

- This method doesn’t currently return any errors, but it might in future

# FinalizedState in zebra_state - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zebra-state/10.0.0/zebra_state/struct.FinalizedState.html

```
pub struct FinalizedState {
    pub db:
```
[ZebraDb](https://docs.rs/struct.ZebraDb.html),
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

The finalized part of the chain state, stored in the db.

`rocksdb` allows concurrent writes through a shared reference,
so clones of the finalized state represent the same database instance.
When the final clone is dropped, the database is closed.

This is different from `NonFinalizedState::clone()`,
which returns an independent copy of the chains.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.db)

`db: `[ZebraDb](https://docs.rs/struct.ZebraDb.html)The underlying database.

`rocksdb` allows reads and writes via a shared reference,
so this database object can be freely cloned.
The last instance that is dropped will close the underlying database.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns an on-disk database instance for `config`, `network`, and `elastic_db`.
If there is no existing database, creates a new database on disk.

Immediately commit a `finalized` block to the finalized state.

This can be called either by the non-finalized state (when finalizing a block) or by the checkpoint verifier.

Use `source` as the source of the block in log messages.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

- Propagates any errors from writing to the DB
- Propagates any errors from updating history and note commitment trees
- If `hashFinalSaplingRoot`/`hashLightClientRoot`/`hashBlockCommitments`does not match the expected value

}## Expand description

A structure with the information needed from the state to build a `getblocktemplate` RPC response.

# LatestChainTip in zebra_state - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zebra-state/10.0.0/zebra_state/struct.LatestChainTip.html

`pub struct LatestChainTip { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Efficient access to the state’s current best chain tip.

Each method returns data from the latest tip, regardless of how many times you call it.

Cloned instances provide identical tip data.

The chain tip data is based on:

- the best non-finalized chain tip, if available, or
- the finalized tip.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

If a lot of blocks are committed at the same time, the latest tip will skip some blocks in the chain.

# NonFinalizedBlocksListener in zebra_state - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zebra-state/10.0.0/zebra_state/struct.NonFinalizedBlocksListener.html

## Expand description

A listener for changes in the non-finalized state.

## Tuple Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.0)

`0: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[Receiver](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/sync/mpsc/bounded/struct.Receiver.html)<([Hash](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/hash/struct.Hash.html), [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[Block](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/struct.Block.html)>)>>## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zebra_state/response.rs.html#267-328)#### pub fn [spawn](https://docs.rs#method.spawn)(
    non_finalized_state_receiver: [WatchReceiver](https://docs.rs/struct.WatchReceiver.html)<[NonFinalizedState](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFinalizedState.html)>,
    known_chain_tips: [HashSet](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/set/struct.HashSet.html)<[Hash](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/hash/struct.Hash.html)>,
) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zebra_state/response.rs.html#267-328)

#### pub fn [spawn](https://docs.rs#method.spawn)(
    non_finalized_state_receiver: [WatchReceiver](https://docs.rs/struct.WatchReceiver.html)<[NonFinalizedState](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFinalizedState.html)>,
    known_chain_tips: [HashSet](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/set/struct.HashSet.html)<[Hash](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/hash/struct.Hash.html)>,
) -> Self

Spawns a task to listen for changes in the non-finalized state and sends any blocks in the non-finalized state to the caller that have not already been sent.

`known_chain_tips` holds the hashes of chain tips the caller already has. On the first send
only, each non-finalized chain is walked from its tip downwards and blocks are sent until a
hash in this set is reached, so any block at or below a known tip on the same chain is
skipped. If it is empty, every block currently in the non-finalized state is sent. After the
first send, those blocks are already tracked as sent, so later sends only forward blocks that
weren’t in the previously seen non-finalized state.

Returns a new instance of [ NonFinalizedBlocksListener](https://docs.rs/struct.NonFinalizedBlocksListener.html) for the caller to listen for new blocks in the non-finalized state.

# NonFinalizedState in zebra_state - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zebra-state/10.0.0/zebra_state/struct.NonFinalizedState.html

```
pub struct NonFinalizedState {
    pub network:
```
[Network](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/parameters/network/enum.Network.html),
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

The state of the chains in memory, including queued blocks.

Clones of the non-finalized state contain independent copies of the chains.
This is different from `FinalizedState::clone()`,
which returns a shared reference to the database.

Most chain data is clone-on-write using [ Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html).

Accepts an optional path to the non-finalized state backup directory and a handle to the database.

If a backup directory path is provided:

- Creates a new backup directory at the provided path if none exists,
- Restores non-finalized blocks from the backup directory, if any, and
- Unless `skip_backup_task`is true, spawns a task that updates the non-finalized backup cache with the latest non-finalized state sent to the returned watch channel.

Returns the non-finalized state with a watch channel sender and receiver.

# ReadStateService in zebra_state - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zebra-state/10.0.0/zebra_state/struct.ReadStateService.html

`pub struct ReadStateService { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A read-only service for accessing Zebra’s cached blockchain state.

This service provides read-only access to:

- the non-finalized state: the most recent blocks, up to
`MAX_BLOCK_REORG_HEIGHT`
- the finalized state: older blocks that have many confirmations.

Requests to this service are processed in parallel,
ignoring any blocks queued by the read-write [`StateService`].

This quick response behavior is better for most state users. It allows other async tasks to make progress while concurrently reading data from disk.

    pub transaction_hashes: [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[[Hash](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transaction/hash/struct.Hash.html)]>,
}## Expand description

A block which has undergone semantic validation and has been prepared for contextual validation.

It is the constructor’s responsibility to perform semantic validation and to ensure that all fields are consistent.

This structure contains data from contextual validation, which is computed in
the *service caller*’s task, not inside the service call itself. This allows
moving work out of the single-threaded state service.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.block)

`block: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[Block](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/struct.Block.html)>The block to commit to the state.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.hash)

`hash: `[Hash](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/hash/struct.Hash.html)The hash of the block.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.height)

`height: `[Height](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/block/height/struct.Height.html)The height of the block.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.new_outputs)

`new_outputs: `[HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html)<[OutPoint](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transparent/struct.OutPoint.html), [OrderedUtxo](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transparent/utxo/struct.OrderedUtxo.html)>New transparent outputs created in this block, indexed by
[ OutPoint](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transparent/struct.OutPoint.html).

Each output is tagged with its transaction index in the block. (The outputs of earlier transactions in a block can be spent by later transactions.)

Note: although these transparent outputs are newly created, they may not be unspent, since a later transaction in a block can spend outputs of an earlier transaction.

This field can also contain unrelated outputs, which are ignored.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.transaction_hashes)

`transaction_hashes: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[[Hash](https://docs.rs/zebra-chain/11.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/zebra_chain/transaction/hash/struct.Hash.html)]>A precomputed list of the hashes of the transactions in this block,
in the same order as `block.transactions`.
